public_rationale: Jia and Liang’s 2017 study used AddSent to add distracting sentences designed to preserve the correct answer [e1]. Average F1 fell from 75.7% to 31.3% across four tested reading-comprehension models [e1]. These results support the historical claim that comparable failures under distracting text were documented in 2017 [e1].
limitations: The study measured reading comprehension in 2017 systems. It does not establish a shared failure mechanism with modern LLMs or an inability to perform formal reasoning.
The answer-preservation method applies to AddSent. The separate AddAny method did not guarantee that additions preserved the correct answer.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that comparable failures under distracting text had already been documented in language-understanding systems in 2017.

Comparable means that adding distracting text reduced correct answers without changing the answer the original passage supported. It does not require identical architectures, tasks, or underlying mechanisms.
The target period is 2017 because the surrounding text explicitly identifies that year's Jia–Liang study.
criteria.support_condition: The 2017 Jia–Liang study reports that adding distracting sentences that preserve the correct answer substantially worsened reading-comprehension model performance.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The cited study found no such deterioration, or its reported failures depended on changing the correct answer rather than adding distracting material.
